plain_level: Grades 9 to 4 are Level 2; grades 3 to 1 are Level 1
what_is_it: The main qualifications taken at school in Years 10 and 11. Graded 9 (highest) to 1: 4 is a standard pass and 5 a strong pass. Without at least a 4 in English and maths, you keep studying them after 16. Mostly exams at the end, and about 120 hours of teaching each.
Two-year courses, usually taken three at a time at a sixth form or college. Graded A* to E, mostly from exams at the end. About 360 hours of teaching each.

plain_level: Level 3, but smaller than an A level
what_is_it: A stand-alone qualification at A level standard, taken on its own or alongside A levels. Graded A to E. AS marks don't count towards an A level.

plain_level: Level 3, the same size as three A levels
what_is_it: A two-year technical course for one area of work, taken after GCSEs. About 80% is in the classroom and 20% on a placement with an employer (45 days). Graded Pass, Merit, Distinction or Distinction*, and worth UCAS points: a Distinction* counts the same as three A levels at A*.

plain_level: Level 1, half the size of a GCSE
what_is_it: The Foundation Project: one piece of work on a topic you choose, often linked to a subject you're studying, taken alongside your GCSEs. You're marked on how well you plan, manage, finish and review it.

plain_level: Level 2, half the size of a GCSE
what_is_it: The Higher Project: one piece of work on a topic you choose, taken alongside your GCSEs, marked on how well you plan, manage, finish and review it. Graded A* to C, like half a GCSE at the same grade.

plain_level: Level 3, half the size of an A level
what_is_it: The Extended Project: a dissertation, investigation, performance or something you make, on a topic that extends a subject you're studying or one you care about. Taken alongside A levels, graded like half an A level, and marked on how well you plan, manage, finish and review it.
Practical English, maths or digital skills for everyday life and work. Pass or fail, by tests and exams.

plain_level: Level 2, the same level as GCSE grades 9 to 4
what_is_it: Practical English or maths for everyday life and work. Pass or fail, by tests and exams. Employers, colleges and apprenticeships widely accept it in place of a GCSE grade 4, but some universities and professional bodies want the GCSE.
Pearson's vocational qualifications, built around an area of work. They come in different sizes, so check the hours on the card: a GCSE is about 120 hours of teaching.

plain_level: Level 2, the same level as GCSE grades 9 to 4
what_is_it: Pearson's vocational qualifications, built around an area of work. They come in different sizes, so check the hours on the card: a GCSE is about 120 hours of teaching.

plain_level: Level 3, the same level as A levels
what_is_it: Pearson's vocational qualifications, built around an area of work, and carrying UCAS points. They come in different sizes, so check the hours on the card: an A level is about 360 hours of teaching. Smaller ones are often taken alongside A levels.

plain_level: Like a GCSE: Level 1 or Level 2, depending on the grade
what_is_it: Pearson's BTEC Tech Awards and Firsts: vocational courses built around an area of work, designed to be as demanding as a GCSE. They come in different sizes, so check the hours on the card: a GCSE is about 120 hours of teaching.
